Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary To win: make words, stay out of the red zone, and have equal scores at the end. To get a better score, make longer words. Words score their length minus 3. At the start of each turn, you draw 3 new cards. Each turn you get 2 actions. For each action, you may: 1. Give a card (click on one of your cards, then click on an arrow to place it there in your partner's hand) 2. Move a card in your partner's hand (click on one of their cards, then click the arrow where you want it to go) 3. Claim a word. Use the up/down arrows to change the letter you are using on each card. Highlight the cards you are using. A word must be spelled out using consecutive cards, using one letter from each card going left to right. If cards are in the wrong place, your partner needs to help you. Words must be 4 letters or longer. At the END of your turn, you need to have 8 or fewer cards. Make sure you're below this limit by claiming words or giving cards away. After the deck is empty, each player gets one last turn to claim a word and/or help their partner make a word. You can also pass. At the end of the game, if the players' scores are equal, you win! Once you have managed to win, try to get a better score. 4-letter words score 1pt 5-letter words score 2pts 6-letter words score 3pts 7-letter words score 4pts and so on. Based on the scores of ONE player (half your combined score): 4-6: a bare success 7-8: good 9-10: great 11-12: Brilliant! 13+: A perfect couple. 18 is the hypothetical maximum score. 15 pts (30 combined) is the best so far. For a list of everyone who has scored 13+, check the forums. [Rating: 3/10] Bad game. The game is luck-driven with not enough mitigation. Beating the game is easy (succeeded in first try) and the only challenge seem to be going for a higher score, which is unsatisfying for a co-op.

[Rating: 4/10] Hard to wrap my head around the top and bottom letters to make words. I probably prefer other word games IMO.

[Rating: 6/10] I honestly dont know how to rate this. it seems hard to win and yet I won 2 out of two games. The concept of helping each others words is nice and at the same time it is somehow cumbersome. i am giving a 6 more on trust than anything but i don't feel like playing it again

[Rating: 6/10] We really struggled with trying to make longer words and keep things balanced. Unfortunately, it was more of a frustrating struggle than a challenging struggle for the other player.

[Rating: 6.5/10] I've been playing a lot of spelling games on BGA lately. The primary feature of this one is that it's cooperative. A player can't move the cards around in his own hand and must rely on his partner to do it on her turns, and even then there is a strict limit on how many cards can be moved. This limitation makes for a challenging puzzle. Interesting game which I'm happy to be playing async and not in-person, as the potential for AP is great.

[Rating: 7/10] Designer Bez invited me to an asynch game of this on BGA (which I didn't log) and then I showed it to Sam, as we both have Wibbell decks already. It's a charming co-op spelling game where each player has to help the other make words from their conveyor belt of letters, and ensure that both players get the same score by the end of the game.

[Rating: 7/10] Interesting take on cooperative games where play is deeply interleaved between the two players, so neither player can perform on their own. Some actions you can only do to your partners board, while others you can only do to your own, and you will need all actions to  succeed. Likely suffers from quarterbacking if played with communication.  It's hard to tell whether the action separation is an innovation or simply a distraction. It's certainly novel.
